questions.q: How does DAMA-DMBOK define a data steward?
options: A business leader and/or subject matter expert accountable for tasks related to data management
Anyone with read access to a database
A piece of software that automatically cleans data
The executive who funds the governance program
questions.explain: DAMA-DMBOK ties stewardship to tasks related to data management, held by someone with business or subject-matter expertise.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three steward flavors described in this lesson?
options: Executive steward
Technical data steward
Business data steward
Data management steward
questions.explain: The three recognized flavors are business, technical, and data management stewards. 'Executive steward' isn't one of them — executive sponsorship (Lesson 18) is a separate role entirely.

questions.q: In the owner/steward relationship, what is the steward's RACI letter?
options: Accountable (A)
Informed (I)
Consulted (C)
Responsible (R)
questions.explain: The owner holds Accountable (A); the steward holds Responsible (R) for the day-to-day work of applying the owner's decisions.

questions.q: A business data steward is primarily focused on:
options: The physical server hardware storing the data
What the data actually means to the business
Writing the company's marketing copy
Negotiating software licensing contracts
questions.explain: The business steward is the one who can answer 'what does this field actually mean' — the technical steward handles structure and storage instead.

questions.q: When a steward can't resolve a data dispute themselves, what should happen?
options: They escalate it to the data owner, who has final approval authority
They should unilaterally change the definition without telling anyone
They should ignore it until someone else notices
The dispute should be sent directly to an external regulator
questions.explain: Escalation to the owner is exactly the point of the owner/steward split — the owner holds the authority to make a final call.
